title: UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026 for Ukrainian Women Refugees and Internally Displaced Women in Ukraine | Fully Funded AI, GIS and Python Training
summary: The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), with generous funding from the Government and People of Japan, has officially opened applications for it s digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026. This fully funded initiative is designed to empower Ukrainian women refugees living in Poland and internally displaced women in Ukraine by equipping them with practical digital skills that can unlock employment opportunities, remote work, entrepreneurship, and long-term economic resilience. As technology continues to reshape industries worldwide, digital skills have become essential for accessing quality jobs and creating sustainable livelihoods. Recognizing this growing need, UNITAR has developed a comprehensive programme that combines technical training, mentoring, coaching, networking, and project development to help participants thrive in the rapidly evolving digital economy. Approximately 500 women will be selected for the first phase of this prestigious programme, with the highest-performing participants advancing to exclusive hackathons and a final conference where they will present innovative projects before employers, investors, donors, and industry experts. About the UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme The programme aims to strengthen the economic security of Ukrainian women who have been displaced due to conflict by providing practical digital education that aligns with today s labour market. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical instruction, participants will gain practical experience through project-based learning, expert mentoring, collaborative workshops, and continuous coaching throughout the programme. Training will be delivered in: Ukrainian Polish English The programme is implemented in partnership with: Polish-Japanese Academy of Information Technology Ukrainian Catholic University Eukarya Additional partner organizations committed to supporting Ukrainian women Why You Should Apply Successful applicants will have the opportunity to: Learn practical Artificial Intelligence (AI) skills. Build expertise in Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Study AI programming using Python. Develop skills for remote employment opportunities. Improve employability in the technology sector. Create innovative digital solutions. Develop entrepreneurial ideas and socially responsible business concepts. Build a professional portfolio. Learn from experienced instructors and mentors. Join an international professional network. Receive continuous coaching throughout the programme. Compete for selection into the virtual hackathon. Earn the opportunity to present projects before employers and investors. Receive an official UNITAR Certificate upon successful completion. Programme Structure The programme consists of three progressive phases that allow participants to continuously develop their technical, entrepreneurial, and leadership skills. Phase I: Online Digital Training Approximately 500 participants will begin with an intensive online learning programme. Every participant will first complete mandatory training in AI Fundamentals before choosing one specialization track. Participants may choose one of the following tracks: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) AI Programming using Python Throughout the online training, participants will: Complete online learning modules. Attend weekly webinars. Participate in consultation sessions. Receive personalized coaching support. Work on practical assignments. Build individual digital projects. Create professional portfolios. Develop self-marketing strategies. Design entrepreneurial or employment-focused project plans. The goal is to ensure every participant finishes Phase I with a practical digital solution or career-ready project. Phase II: Virtual Hackathon and Workshop Up to 75 top-performing participants will advance to the second phase. Selected participants will: Work collaboratively in virtual teams. Solve real-world challenges. Participate in an intensive virtual hackathon. Receive guidance from mentors and industry professionals. Refine projects developed during Phase I. Improve digital solutions using expert feedback. Strengthen business concepts and entrepreneurial ideas. This phase emphasizes teamwork, innovation, creativity, and practical problem-solving. Phase III: Final Conference Approximately 30 outstanding participants will qualify for the final stage. During this prestigious conference, participants will: Present polished projects. Pitch business ideas. Showcase digital solutions. Engage with employers. Network with investors. Meet donors. Receive additional mentoring. Build leadership skills. Improve communication and presentation techniques. Learn financial planning. Conduct market research for their projects. The conference provides an excellent platform for participants to gain visibility and establish valuable professional relationships. Learning Objectives Upon successful completion of the programme, participants will be able to: Apply Artificial Intelligence tools to practical workplace challenges. Improve employability through digital competencies. Use GIS technology to solve real-world problems. Develop AI applications using Python programming. Create digital solutions that address societal challenges. Build professional portfolios. Design project plans. Develop self-marketing strategies. Create socially responsible business concepts. Assess the feasibility and market potential of digital innovations. Collaborate effectively with mentors and peers. Incorporate professional feedback into project development. Deliver compelling project presentations. Demonstrate improved leadership abilities. Strengthen communication skills. Increase confidence in digital technologies. Prepare for careers in technology and entrepreneurship. Who Can Apply? Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements: Be a Ukrainian woman refugee registered in Poland or an internally displaced woman living in Ukraine. Be at least 18 years old. Have an interest in digital technologies. Be motivated to learn through practical experience. Possess basic computer literacy. Have basic mathematics skills. Have access to a computer. Have reliable internet access. Be able to dedicate sufficient time to complete the intensive online programme. Be interested in entering the technology industry or upgrading existing digital skills. Preferred Qualifications Applicants are encouraged—but not required—to have: University education. Beginner-level knowledge in an IT-related field. Importantly, no previous programming experience is required , making the programme accessible to beginners who are eager to learn. Certification Participants who successfully complete the programme and satisfy all performance requirements will receive an official UNITAR Certificate . Training will be delivered through a dedicated digital learning hub that supports: Online learning. Professional networking. Peer collaboration. Resource sharing. Continued access to digital-sector information after programme completion. About the UNITAR-Japan Partnership This initiative is made possible through the long-standing partnership between UNITAR and the Government and People of Japan. The partnership focuses on strengthening resilience, promoting sustainable development, and supporting vulnerable populations through capacity-building initiatives. Through this programme, displaced Ukrainian women will receive practical digital education that enhances their economic independence while creating opportunities for sustainable employment and entrepreneurship. Why This Programme Matters Digital transformation is creating unprecedented opportunities across industries. However, displaced populations often face significant barriers to accessing quality employment and professional development. This programme directly addresses these challenges by combining technical education with mentoring, coaching, networking, and project development. Rather than simply teaching digital concepts, UNITAR provides participants with practical experience and professional exposure that can significantly improve their career prospects. For women seeking to rebuild their lives through technology, this programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain internationally recognized training, expand professional networks, and develop innovative projects with guidance from experts. Application Deadline 25 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline, as late submissions may not be considered. APPLY HERE For more information about this opportunity visit the UNITAR website HERE Also visit the OFY Website HERE for more global opportunities Conclusion The UNITAR Digital Upskilling and Reskilling Programme 2026 represents a valuable opportunity for Ukrainian women refugees in Poland and internally displaced women in Ukraine to acquire in-demand digital skills without financial barriers. Through comprehensive training in Artificial Intelligence, GIS, and Python programming, participants will strengthen their employability, build entrepreneurial capacity, and gain access to mentoring, networking, and career development opportunities. With its structured learning pathway, practical project work, international partnerships, and official certification, the programme provides participants with the knowledge and confidence needed to pursue meaningful careers in today s rapidly evolving digital economy. Interested applicants should ensure they submit their applications before 25 August 2026 to be considered for this transformative opportunity. title: Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships 2027 in Australia: Receive Up to AUD 180,000 to Scale Innovative Social and Environmental Solution
summary: The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships are now accepting Expressions of Interest from exceptional Australian innovators who are developing transformative solutions to some of Australia s most urgent social and environmental challenges. Established by the Sidney Myer Fund and The Myer Foundation , the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships provide outstanding individuals with the time, financial support, expert guidance, mentorship, and professional network needed to significantly expand the impact of their innovative initiatives. Unlike many funding opportunities that focus on delivering predetermined outputs or strict performance indicators, this Fellowship is designed to give talented innovators the freedom to dedicate twelve months exclusively to advancing existing high-impact projects that demonstrate strong potential for lasting societal and environmental change. Each selected Fellow receives funding of up to AUD 180,000 over a twelve-month period, allowing them to step away from their regular employment and fully concentrate on developing innovative solutions capable of creating meaningful and scalable impact across Australia. About the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships were established to encourage bold thinking, innovative leadership, and entrepreneurial approaches to addressing complex societal issues. The Fellowship recognizes that many groundbreaking ideas require dedicated time, financial security, mentorship, and strategic support before they can reach their full potential. Rather than funding organizations, the Fellowship invests directly in individuals whose ideas have already demonstrated traction and are ready to move to the next stage of development. Successful Fellows become part of a growing network of innovators who are committed to creating sustainable, long-term solutions that benefit Australian communities. Fellowship Themes Applicants must propose projects aligned with one or more of the following priority themes: Inclusion Equality Sustainability Environment, including Climate Change Human, Civil Legal Rights Projects should clearly demonstrate how they contribute to solving major challenges within these focus areas. Fellowship Benefits Each successful Fellow may receive funding worth up to AUD 180,000 , including: 1. Personal Fellowship Stipend Recipients receive: AUD 140,000 stipend Financial support throughout the twelve-month Fellowship Opportunity to dedicate full-time attention to their project 2. Project Funding An additional up to AUD 40,000 is available for approved project-related expenses, including: Renting dedicated workspace Professional travel Hiring external consultants or specialists Other approved Fellowship-related costs Project expenses are reimbursed based on approved expenditure. 3. Professional Development Support Beyond funding, Fellows gain access to: Quarterly meetings with a panel of experienced experts One-on-one mentorship Networking opportunities with previous Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellows Guidance from Fellowship staff and advisors Access to an influential innovation community Who Should Apply? The Fellowship welcomes individuals from diverse professional backgrounds, sectors, and lived experiences. Applicants are encouraged to submit an Expression of Interest if they are leading innovative projects capable of delivering significant social or environmental impact. Ideal Projects Projects should be: High-impact Innovative or uniquely applied Capable of generating measurable outcomes Scalable Sustainable over time Focused on addressing significant Australian challenges Innovation may involve creating entirely new approaches or adapting proven ideas to new contexts. Ideal Applicants Strong applicants typically demonstrate: Significant experience in their field Entrepreneurial thinking A proven record of achievement Passion for their cause Strong professional networks Curiosity and willingness to learn Ability to collaborate effectively Commitment to making the most of the Fellowship experience Eligibility Requirements To qualify, applicants must: Be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. Reside in Australia for most of the Fellowship period. Be willing to take a twelve-month sabbatical from their current role. Demonstrate a strong history of achievement. Show entrepreneurial and innovative thinking. Be capable of transforming ideas into practical action. Have established networks related to their project. Project Eligibility Requirements Eligible projects must: Be based in Australia. Align with one or more Fellowship themes. Have been in development for no longer than three years . What Fellows Are Expected to Do The Fellowship is intentionally flexible. Rather than requiring recipients to meet rigid performance targets, Fellows are encouraged to use the year to advance their initiatives thoughtfully and strategically. During the Fellowship, recipients are expected to: Focus full-time on their project. Participate in Fellowship activities. Engage with mentors and advisors. Present a mid-term progress update. Deliver a final presentation at the conclusion of the Fellowship. Funding Exclusions The Fellowship does not support: Projects older than three years. Academic research projects. Higher degree coursework or dissertations. Medical research. Disease-specific initiatives. International projects. Scholarships. Sponsorships. Funding hubs or accelerator programs. Creative arts projects. Collaborative applications involving multiple individuals. Organizational applications. Capital campaigns. Endowment campaigns. Fundraising events. Program or service delivery projects without innovation potential. Curriculum or education development projects for schools, universities, or educational institutions. Application Process The Fellowship follows a multi-stage selection process designed to identify Australia s most promising innovators. Stage 1: Expression of Interest Applicants submit an online Expression of Interest (EOI) during the application window. Stage 2: Initial Review Following the closing date, applications undergo an extensive assessment process. Stage 3: Shortlisting Selected applicants are invited to prepare a detailed application. Stage 4: Interviews Shortlisted candidates participate in interviews. Stage 5: Final Selection Successful Fellows are confirmed following completion of the interview process. 2027 Application Timeline Applicants should carefully note the official timeline: 13 July 2026 – Expressions of Interest open. 16 August 2026 (11:59 PM AEST) – Expressions of Interest close. Week beginning 19 October 2026 – Shortlisted candidates invited to submit detailed applications. 10 January 2027 (11:59 PM AEDT) – Detailed applications due. February 2027 – Interviews conducted. March 2027 – Successful Fellows announced. Late submissions will not be accepted under any circumstances, including technical difficulties or personal issues. Applicants are also not permitted to submit additional materials after the application deadline. APPLY HERE For more information about this opportunity visit the Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships website HERE You can visit OFY Website HERE for more fellowship programs Recent Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellows The Fellowship has supported numerous innovators addressing pressing national issues. Alicia Kennedy Founder of Cherished Pets , Alicia Kennedy is developing the Human-Animal Bond ecosystem of care (HABCare), integrating veterinary care with housing, health, and social services to improve wellbeing for vulnerable Australians. Campbell Costello Founder of Bush Labs , Campbell Costello is expanding access to portable PCR diagnostic technology for animal diseases in remote and underserved regions, strengthening disease surveillance, food security, and public health. Zanab Malik Founder of My Special Needs Dental Home , Zanab Malik is creating a digital platform that equips carers and support workers with specialist oral health guidance for Australians living with profound disabilities. These examples demonstrate the Fellowship s commitment to supporting innovative ideas with the potential to create nationwide impact. Why Apply? The Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships represent one of Australia s premier opportunities for innovators seeking the resources and freedom to expand transformative ideas. Recipients receive generous financial support, mentorship, professional guidance, expert advice, and access to an influential community of previous Fellows, enabling them to focus entirely on scaling initiatives that can improve lives and strengthen Australian society. If you have an innovative project addressing inclusion, environmental sustainability, climate action, or human rights, this Fellowship provides a unique platform to accelerate your work and maximize long-term impact. Deadline Expression of Interest Deadline: 16 August 2026 (11:59 PM AEST) Late applications will not be accepted. Conclusion The 2027 Kenneth Myer Innovation Fellowships offer a rare opportunity for Australia s most innovative changemakers to dedicate an entire year to advancing bold ideas capable of solving significant social and environmental challenges. With funding of up to AUD 180,000 , extensive mentoring, strategic guidance, and access to a powerful network of innovators, the Fellowship is designed to help individuals transform promising initiatives into sustainable, scalable solutions that deliver lasting benefits across Australia. Eligible innovators are encouraged to carefully review the eligibility criteria and submit their Expression of Interest before the application deadline of 16 August 2026 . title: CDC Research Participation Opportunities Through ORISE: Explore Current Openings for Students, Graduates and Faculty
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Research Participation Program offers current students, recent graduates and eligible university faculty an opportunity to explore research experiences connected to the work of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The programme is administered through the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education , commonly known as ORISE. Available opportunities are published in an online catalogue and managed through Zintellect , ORISE’s application-management platform. Rather than advertising one single position, the programme provides access to a changing collection of research opportunities. Applicants should visit the official catalogue regularly, use the available filters and review each listing separately to identify projects that match their academic background, research interests and professional goals. Applications are accepted throughout the year, and additional opportunities are added regularly. However, each individual position may have its own eligibility requirements, application instructions and closing date. About the CDC Research Participation Program The CDC Research Participation Program connects eligible applicants with research opportunities associated with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The programme may be relevant to people seeking practical research exposure, experience in a public-health environment or opportunities to apply academic knowledge to real-world scientific and policy questions. Because the programme contains multiple listings rather than a single recruitment cycle, applicants may find opportunities covering different subjects, locations, educational levels and research areas. The specific responsibilities, duration and qualifications will depend on the individual opportunity selected from the catalogue. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that all CDC research opportunities have the same conditions. Every listing should be read carefully before an application is submitted. Who Should Explore the Current CDC Research Opportunities? The official programme information states that applications are accepted from: Current students Recent graduates Faculty members at United States colleges and universities These categories are broad, and the exact academic or professional requirements may differ from one opportunity to another. For example, one project may be designed for undergraduate students, while another may require a graduate degree, specialised laboratory training or experience in a particular research field. Some opportunities may be suitable for applicants in areas such as: Public health Epidemiology Biological sciences Laboratory research Environmental health Data science Statistics Behavioural and social sciences Health communication Medicine Health policy Other related disciplines These subject areas are examples of fields that may be relevant to CDC-related research. Applicants must rely on the official description of each individual opportunity to confirm whether their background is suitable. How the Opportunities Catalogue Works The ORISE website provides an online catalogue of current CDC research opportunities. Applicants can browse the catalogue and use search or filtering functions to identify positions that match their qualifications and interests. Each listing should normally provide the information needed to decide whether to apply, such as: Project title Research area Host office or programme Required education Applicant eligibility Location or participation format Expected activities Application deadline Required documents Opportunity number Contact details The exact information available may differ between listings. Applicants should click the title of an opportunity to open its full description rather than relying only on the summary displayed in the catalogue. Why Applicants Should Check the Website Regularly CDC research opportunities are available throughout the year, and new listings may be added at different times. There is no single annual deadline covering every position. An applicant who does not find a suitable opportunity during one visit may find a relevant new listing later. For this reason, interested candidates should check the catalogue regularly. It may be helpful to search using several combinations of keywords, including: Academic discipline Research technique Degree level Public-health topic Geographic location CDC programme area Applicants should also review opportunities slightly outside their main specialisation. A position may require transferable skills in research, data analysis, writing or project support even when its title does not exactly match the applicant’s degree. Using Zintellect to Apply Applications are managed through Zintellect , ORISE’s online application system. To apply for any listed CDC research opportunity, candidates must first create a Zintellect profile. To visit the official Zintellect website, CLICK HERE . Once an account has been created, applicants can use the platform to: Review available opportunities Open full project descriptions Prepare an applicant profile Upload supporting documents Submit applications Monitor the status of submitted applications Apply to additional opportunities when eligible Applicants should ensure that the information entered into their profile is complete and accurate. A partially completed profile may delay an application or make it more difficult to demonstrate eligibility. Step-by-Step Application Process 1. Visit the Official Opportunities Catalogue Begin by reviewing the current CDC research opportunities on the ORISE website. Use the catalogue’s search and filter functions to identify relevant listings. 2. Read the Full Opportunity Description Click the title of the position and examine all sections carefully. Pay particular attention to: Eligibility Required qualifications Research duties Educational level Location Application deadline Required documents Do not apply based only on the title. 3. Record the Opportunity Number Each opportunity may have a reference or opportunity number. Applicants should save this number because it may be required when contacting ORISE with questions. 4. Create a Zintellect Account Candidates who do not already have an account must create a profile at Zintellect. Complete all requested sections before beginning the application. 5. Prepare the Required Documents The exact requirements will be stated in the selected listing. Depending on the opportunity, applicants may be asked to submit documents such as: Curriculum vitae or résumé Academic transcripts Personal or research statement Cover letter References Recommendation letters Proof of enrolment Proof of degree completion Writing or research samples Applicants should not assume that the same documents are required for every position. 6. Submit Before the Individual Deadline Although programme opportunities are advertised throughout the year, individual listings may close on specific dates. Applicants should submit early and verify that all uploaded documents are readable and complete. 7. Monitor the Application After submitting, candidates should continue checking their Zintellect account and email for updates, requests or further instructions. Important Points to Check Before Applying Because the catalogue contains multiple research opportunities, conditions may vary significantly. Applicants should verify the following for every listing: Eligibility Confirm whether the opportunity is open to current students, recent graduates, faculty members or another specified group. Degree Requirements Check whether the listing requires an undergraduate, master’s, doctoral or professional degree. Graduation Window Some opportunities for recent graduates may define how recently the applicant must have completed their degree. Citizenship or Residency Requirements The general programme summary provided does not state one universal citizenship rule for every opportunity. Applicants must check each listing for any citizenship, residency, visa or work-authorisation conditions. Location and Participation Format Determine whether the opportunity is: In person Remote Hybrid Based at a particular CDC site Connected to another approved research location Deadline There is no single deadline for the whole catalogue. Each position may have its own closing date. Financial and Appointment Conditions The general information provided does not specify a standard stipend, salary, benefits package or appointment duration. Applicants should review the individual opportunity description for any available information about financial support and programme conditions. Technical Support Applicants experiencing technical difficulties with Zintellect may contact: Zintellect Support: Zintellect@orau.org When requesting support, applicants should describe the technical issue clearly. Questions about a particular research opportunity should include the relevant opportunity number so that ORISE staff can identify the correct listing. Application Deadline There is no single universal application deadline for all CDC Research Participation Program opportunities. Applications are accepted throughout the year, and new opportunities are added regularly. However, individual listings may have specific deadlines. Applicants must follow the date stated in the opportunity they intend to apply for. Conclusion The CDC Research Participation Program provides a central route for students, recent graduates and eligible faculty members to explore research opportunities connected to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Because the programme includes a regularly updated catalogue of separate positions, applicants should search the official website frequently and review each opportunity on its own terms. The most important first step is to create a complete Zintellect profile. Candidates can then explore available projects, compare eligibility requirements and apply directly to opportunities that match their academic and professional background. The catalogue may change throughout the year, so the absence of a suitable opening today does not mean that another relevant opportunity will not appear tomorrow. Research careers are occasionally built through grand discoveries—but often they begin with the less glamorous art of checking the right webpage at the right time. For current CDC research opportunities, visit the official ORISE opportunities catalogue and select the title of any listing to view its complete description. For more information about this opportunity, VISIT HERE . To create an account and submit applications, VISIT HERE . title: Fully Funded DKFZ PhD Position 2026 in Translational Cancer Biology at LMU Munich
summary: The German Cancer Research Center is accepting applications for a fully funded PhD position in Translational Cancer Biology at the German Cancer Consortium partner site in Munich, Germany. The three-year doctoral position will investigate the molecular mechanisms that drive the progression, metastasis and therapy resistance of small cell lung cancer. The successful candidate will combine experimental cancer biology with functional genomics, advanced disease models and computational analysis of large-scale sequencing data. The position is located in the Department of Translational Oncology at the DKTK partner site Munich, based at the LMU Klinikum Großhadern. The successful applicant is expected to begin in November 2026 and will become part of the DKFZ International PhD Program. Applicants should hold a master’s degree in molecular medicine, human biology, biochemistry, biology or another closely related life-science discipline. Practical experience in molecular biology and mammalian cell culture is required. The application deadline is 11 August 2026 . About the German Cancer Research Center The German Cancer Research Center, commonly known as DKFZ, is one of Europe’s largest cancer research institutions. Its mission, “Research for a life without cancer,” reflects its commitment to understanding the causes and biological mechanisms of cancer and translating scientific discoveries into improved prevention, diagnosis and treatment. DKFZ brings together researchers working across multiple scientific disciplines, including: Molecular and cellular biology Cancer genetics and epigenetics Functional genomics Computational biology Immunology Medical imaging Epidemiology Translational oncology Clinical cancer research Researchers at DKFZ work within an international scientific environment supported by advanced technologies, specialist infrastructure and global research partnerships. The institution aims to create conditions in which fundamental scientific discoveries can be transformed into practical benefits for patients and public health. About the German Cancer Consortium DKFZ works with selected university medical centres through the German Cancer Consortium, known as DKTK. DKFZ acts as the core centre of the consortium, while partner sites are located in: Berlin Dresden Essen and Düsseldorf Frankfurt and Mainz Freiburg Heidelberg Munich Tübingen The consortium operates joint translational research centres at university medical institutions across these locations. Its purpose is to narrow the gap between basic laboratory science and clinical cancer care. DKTK researchers develop and evaluate new approaches to personalised oncology, including strategies related to: Cancer prevention Early diagnosis Molecular classification Targeted treatment Therapy-response prediction Drug resistance Translational research Clinical application The consortium also supports the education of future medical, clinical and translational scientists and helps establish research pipelines connecting laboratory discoveries with clinical research and wider healthcare innovation. About the PhD Position in Translational Cancer Biology The PhD project is based in the Department of Translational Oncology at the DKTK partner site Munich. The selected doctoral researcher will join a project investigating small cell lung cancer, an aggressive form of lung cancer associated with rapid progression, metastasis and frequent treatment resistance. The project seeks to understand how molecular and epigenetic regulatory mechanisms influence the behaviour of small cell lung cancer cells. A particular focus will be placed on MYC-dependent transcriptional and epigenetic regulation of enhancer networks . Enhancers are regulatory regions of DNA that help control gene expression. Changes in enhancer activity can alter which genes are activated or suppressed in cancer cells. These changes may contribute to tumour development, metastatic behaviour and resistance to treatment. The project will examine how MYC-dependent enhancer regulation shapes gene-expression programmes associated with: Tumour progression Metastasis Cancer-cell identity Therapy response Treatment resistance Potential therapeutic vulnerabilities By identifying biological dependencies within these regulatory networks, the research may help reveal new treatment targets for patients with small cell lung cancer. Translational Focus of the Research The project is designed to connect mechanistic laboratory research with clinically relevant cancer models. The doctoral researcher will work with patient-derived systems and preclinical models that more closely reflect the complexity of human disease. This translational approach is intended to ensure that discoveries made in the laboratory are relevant to future treatment strategies. The research will combine: Molecular biology Cell biology Biochemistry Functional genomics Genome engineering Three-dimensional cancer models Genetically engineered mouse models Multi-omics analysis Computational interpretation of sequencing data Although the project includes computational components, its primary focus is experimental laboratory research. Main Responsibilities Conduct Molecular and Cellular Experiments The PhD student will perform molecular biology, cell biology and biochemical experiments using human and murine small cell lung cancer models. This may involve studying: Gene expression Protein function Cellular signalling Cancer-cell proliferation Tumour-cell survival Metastatic behaviour Therapy response Molecular resistance mechanisms The researcher will be expected to design experiments carefully, maintain accurate records, interpret results and troubleshoot technical challenges. Apply CRISPR-Based Genome Engineering The successful candidate will use CRISPR-based genome-engineering tools to investigate genes and regulatory elements involved in small cell lung cancer. CRISPR approaches may be used to: Disrupt selected genes Modify regulatory regions Test gene function Identify cancer dependencies Examine enhancer activity Conduct functional genetic screens Experience with CRISPR is not explicitly listed as mandatory, but applicants should demonstrate a willingness to develop expertise in genome engineering and functional screening. Develop Advanced Three-Dimensional Cancer Models The PhD student will help establish and characterise advanced three-dimensional cancer models. These models may better reproduce tumour structure and cancer-cell interactions than conventional two-dimensional cell culture. Relevant systems may include: Organoids Spheroids Patient-derived models Other advanced in vitro cancer platforms The researcher will use these models to investigate tumour biology and treatment response under clinically relevant conditions. Work With Genetically Engineered Mouse Models The project includes work with genetically engineered mouse models of small cell lung cancer. Applicants should therefore be interested in animal-based cancer research and willing to learn the relevant experimental, ethical and regulatory procedures. Previous experience with mouse models is desirable but is not stated as an absolute requirement. Analyse Multi-Omics Data The researcher will help integrate and interpret multiple types of genomic and transcriptomic data. The datasets may include: Bulk RNA sequencing Single-cell RNA sequencing Spatial transcriptomics ChIP sequencing ATAC sequencing Bulk RNA sequencing measures gene-expression patterns across a population of cells, while single-cell RNA sequencing provides information at the level of individual cells. Spatial transcriptomics helps researchers examine where gene-expression patterns occur within tissues. ChIP sequencing and ATAC sequencing can provide information about protein-DNA interactions, chromatin accessibility and regulatory activity. The PhD student is not necessarily expected to enter the project as an advanced computational scientist. However, interest in learning computational methods is important, and basic experience in genomic-data analysis would strengthen an application. Present and Publish Research Findings The doctoral researcher will be expected to communicate findings through: Research-group meetings Departmental seminars National conferences International conferences Scientific manuscripts Collaborative publications The successful candidate will contribute to high-impact scientific publications and participate in collaborations with leading cancer-research groups. Required Academic Qualifications Applicants must hold a master’s degree in a relevant life-science field. Suitable disciplines include: Molecular medicine Human biology Biochemistry Biology Molecular biology Biomedical sciences Cancer biology Biotechnology A closely related life-science discipline The master’s qualification should provide sufficient preparation for experimental doctoral research in molecular and translational cancer biology. Required Research Experience Applicants should have practical experience in: Molecular biology Mammalian cell culture Laboratory-based experimental research Candidates should clearly describe the techniques they have used during their degree, thesis, research assistantship or previous employment. Relevant experience may include: DNA and RNA extraction PCR or quantitative PCR Cloning Western blotting Immunofluorescence Gene-expression analysis Cell viability assays Transfection Microscopy Protein analysis Mammalian cell-line maintenance The vacancy does not state that applicants must already be experts in every method used by the project. Desired Skills and Interests The ideal candidate will demonstrate: Strong interest in translational cancer research Interest in molecular mechanisms of gene regulation Curiosity about cancer progression and treatment resistance Willingness to work with mouse models Interest in computational analysis of genomic datasets Ability to work independently Strong motivation Collaborative and team-oriented behaviour Excellent written and spoken English Basic computational or bioinformatics experience is desirable but not mandatory. Candidates should be prepared to work in an interdisciplinary environment where experimental and computational researchers collaborate closely. DKFZ International PhD Program The successful candidate will join the DKFZ International PhD Program. The programme provides structured doctoral training alongside the candidate’s research project. Support may include: Scientific mentoring Professional-development opportunities Transferable-skills training Career guidance Research seminars International networking Access to DKFZ Career Service activities Opportunities to engage with doctoral researchers from different disciplines The programme is intended to help candidates develop both as independent scientists and as professionals capable of pursuing careers in academia, healthcare, biotechnology or related fields. Research Environment in Munich The position is based at the Department of Translational Oncology at LMU Klinikum Großhadern in Munich. The successful candidate will work in a collaborative environment with access to facilities and expertise at both: The German Cancer Research Center Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität Munich This arrangement provides access to basic, translational and clinical research communities. The doctoral researcher will benefit from: Modern laboratory infrastructure Advanced imaging technologies Genome-engineering platforms Next-generation sequencing Organoid and three-dimensional model systems Specialist core facilities Computational expertise Clinical research connections International collaborations Funding and Employment Conditions The position is fully funded for an initial period of three years. The selected candidate will receive a doctoral salary together with the usual applicable social benefits. The exact salary amount is not specified in the vacancy information provided. Additional employment conditions include: Thirty days of annual vacation Flexible working hours Possible mobile-working arrangements where compatible with the role Possible part-time arrangements Family-friendly working conditions A subsidised Germany job ticket for public transport Access to international research networks Training and mentoring Career-development support Corporate health-management services Because the project is primarily laboratory-based, any mobile-working arrangement will necessarily depend on experimental responsibilities. Expected Start Date and Duration The position is expected to begin in: November 2026 The appointment is initially limited to: Three years Applicants should be available to relocate to, or work in, Munich for the duration of the doctoral project. Diversity and Equal Opportunity DKFZ welcomes applications from talented candidates regardless of: Gender Cultural background Nationality Ethnicity Sexual identity Physical ability Religion Age Candidates with severe disabilities will receive preference where they have equal suitability for the position. The vacancy does not state any nationality restriction, meaning international applicants may apply subject to the relevant admission, visa and employment requirements. Measles-Immunity Requirement DKFZ is subject to the German Infection Protection Act. All employees must therefore provide proof of immunity against measles. Applicants should be prepared to submit the required medical or vaccination documentation if selected. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the official DKFZ online recruitment system. Applications sent by email will not be accepted. DKFZ also states that application documents submitted by post cannot be returned. Applicants should prepare materials that clearly demonstrate: Their relevant master’s degree Laboratory experience in molecular biology Mammalian cell-culture experience Interest in translational cancer research Motivation to study small cell lung cancer Ability to work independently and collaboratively English-language proficiency Any experience with CRISPR, mouse models or genomic-data analysis The vacancy information does not list every required application document. Candidates should consult the official online portal for the complete submission requirements. APPLY HERE Contact Information Questions about the scientific project may be directed to: Dr Lisa Fröhlich Telephone: (0)89 4400-43962 Applications should not be sent to this contact by email. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 11 August 2026 Candidates should complete the online application before the final day to avoid technical problems. Conclusion The DKFZ PhD position in Translational Cancer Biology offers a fully funded opportunity to investigate the molecular mechanisms driving small cell lung cancer progression, metastasis and therapy resistance. title: National Geographic Society & The Nature Conservancy Community Conservation, Data Visualization, and Mapping Externship 2026: Fully Remote 8-Week Global Opportunity with $500 Stipend for Young Conservation Leaders

Running for eight weeks , the externship offers a flexible schedule requiring approximately 10 hours per week , making it suitable for students and young professionals who want to gain valuable international experience while balancing their studies or other commitments. Solving these challenges requires innovative thinkers who can use science, technology, data, and storytelling to create meaningful change. The National Geographic Society and The Nature Conservancy have partnered to launch this unique externship to equip young people with practical conservation skills while empowering them to address environmental challenges within their own communities. Conservation Storytelling Using Esri StoryMaps, participants will create engaging digital stories that combine: Maps Images Research Geographic information Environmental narratives These projects become valuable portfolio pieces for future academic and professional opportunities. Systems Thinking Participants will explore how global environmental challenges affect local ecosystems and communities while developing solutions that connect local action with broader conservation goals. Its mission focuses on protecting the lands and waters upon which all life depends while addressing: Climate change Biodiversity conservation Sustainable ecosystems Community resilience The organization works globally to create a future where both people and nature thrive. title: NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 in the USA | Up to $250,000 for Humanities Research Projects
summary: The National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) is inviting applications for its Collaborative Research Grants 2026, a prestigious funding opportunity designed to advance knowledge in the humanities through collaborative scholarship. The program supports teams of researchers working together on projects that produce significant interpretive outputs such as books, digital publications, scholarly websites, peer-reviewed journal issues, and other sustainable research resources. With awards of up to $250,000 , this funding opportunity provides scholars and institutions with the resources needed to pursue innovative humanities research that contributes to a deeper understanding of the history and culture of the United States and Western civilization. About the NEH Collaborative Research Program The Collaborative Research Program supports teams of scholars engaged in humanities research that addresses important research questions through collaborative approaches. Projects may be based within a single discipline or bring together expertise from multiple fields. NEH encourages projects that: * Advance humanities scholarship. * Incorporate diverse perspectives and approaches. * Explore new areas of inquiry. * Foster interdisciplinary collaboration. * Produce tangible and sustainable scholarly outputs. Collaborators may come from a single institution or multiple institutions, and international partnerships are welcome provided that scholars at U.S. institutions make substantial contributions to the project. Funding Categories The 2026 competition supports three project categories: 1. Planning International Collaboration Supports the development of international humanities research partnerships and collaborative projects. Maximum Award: Up to $50,000 2. Manuscript Preparation Supports collaborative research leading to scholarly books, edited volumes, and peer-reviewed publications. 3. Scholarly Digital Project Supports the creation of digital humanities resources, databases, websites, and digital publications that advance humanities scholarship. Funding Benefits Successful applicants may receive: * Funding of up to $250,000 depending on project category. * Support for collaborative humanities research. * Resources for manuscript development and publication. * Funding for digital humanities projects. * Opportunities to establish international research partnerships. * Support for interdisciplinary and cross-institutional collaboration. Expected Project Outputs Projects must result in a tangible and sustainable product, including: * Co-authored books * Edited scholarly volumes * Themed issues of peer-reviewed journals * Digital publications * Scholarly websites * Digital humanities resources Outputs should demonstrate meaningful collaboration and contribute to significant humanities research questions. Eligible Applicants The program is open to organizations and institutions supporting humanities research teams. Collaborators may come from: * Universities and colleges * Research institutions * Cultural organizations * Humanities centers * Nonprofit organizations International collaboration is encouraged, but U.S.-based scholars must play a significant role in the project. 2026 Program Priority For the 2026 funding cycle, proposed projects must focus on: * The history of the United States * The culture of the United States * Western civilization Applicants should ensure that their projects align clearly with these thematic priorities. Project Duration Depending on the funding category, projects may receive support for up to: Three Years This allows research teams sufficient time to complete substantial humanities projects and produce high-quality scholarly outputs. Application Timeline | Application Opens | July 7, 2026 | | Application Deadline | September 16, 2026 | Applicants are encouraged to begin preparations early to allow sufficient time for institutional approvals and registration requirements. Application Process Step 1: Review the Funding Opportunity Carefully read the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and related application guidance documents. Step 2: Complete Required Registrations Applicants must have active registrations with: * SAM.gov * Grants.gov Organizations should verify that their registrations are current before beginning the application process. Step 3: Prepare the Application Develop a strong proposal that clearly outlines: * Research objectives * Collaborative structure * Project methodology * Expected outcomes * Dissemination plans Step 4: Submit Through Grants.gov Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov before the deadline. Why Apply? The NEH Collaborative Research Grants represent one of the leading funding opportunities for humanities scholars seeking to undertake ambitious collaborative research projects. Whether developing a major scholarly publication, creating innovative digital resources, or building international partnerships, this program provides the financial support needed to generate lasting contributions to humanities scholarship. The program also encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and supports projects that bring together diverse expertise to address complex research questions in new and meaningful ways. Contact Information Division of Research National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) 📧 [collaborative@neh.gov](mailto:collaborative@neh.gov) 📞 202-606-8200 Conclusion The NEH Collaborative Research Grants 2026 offer a remarkable opportunity for humanities researchers and institutions to collaborate on projects that expand knowledge, generate impactful scholarship, and contribute to a deeper understanding of the United States and Western civilization. With funding of up to $250,000, support for international collaboration, and opportunities to create lasting scholarly resources, this program is ideal for teams seeking to advance innovative humanities research. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals now and submit their applications before the September 16, 2026 deadline. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji: Complete Guide to the 2026 National UN Volunteer Opportunity in Suva

The assignment offers professionals an opportunity to work directly with UNICEF s Communication Section, supporting advocacy campaigns, multimedia storytelling, digital communications, donor visibility initiatives, and audience engagement across 14 Pacific Island countries. title: Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 in South Africa: Fully Supported Master’s, Doctoral and Postdoctoral Funding for Outstanding Researchers
summary: The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust (OMT) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Postgraduate Scholarships for students planning to begin their studies between January and June 2027 . The Trust continues its long-standing commitment to developing exceptional academic talent by supporting outstanding scholars pursuing Master s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies in South Africa and, in exceptional cases, internationally. The scholarship is designed for individuals with an exceptional academic record who aspire to make significant contributions to academia, scientific research, innovation, development, public policy, and other fields that advance knowledge and benefit society. Every year, the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust awards a limited number of highly competitive scholarships to scholars who demonstrate excellence, leadership potential, and a commitment to using their advanced education to contribute meaningfully to South Africa s future. Applications for students intending to commence studies between January and June 2027 are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026 . About the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust is one of South Africa s leading philanthropic organizations dedicated to supporting higher education, research, youth development, and initiatives that strengthen the country s knowledge economy. Through its postgraduate scholarship programme, the Trust invests in future academics, researchers, innovators, and professionals whose work has the potential to address national and global challenges. The scholarship programme has supported numerous distinguished researchers and scholars whose work has gained international recognition across multiple disciplines. The Trust believes that investing in highly talented individuals contributes directly to strengthening South Africa s research capacity, universities, innovation ecosystem, and long-term development. OMT Postgraduate Scholarship Programme 2027 The scholarship programme supports postgraduate studies at three academic levels: Master s Degree Doctoral (PhD) Degree Postdoctoral Research Each year, only a limited number of scholarships are awarded, making the programme highly competitive. Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional academic achievement together with clear plans for using their education to contribute to research, teaching, development, or other knowledge-driven sectors. International Study Opportunities The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust also provides funding for international postgraduate study , although this opportunity is reserved only for exceptional candidates. Applicants seeking international scholarships must demonstrate one or more of the following: Their proposed programme is in a unique or highly specialized discipline that is not readily available in South Africa. The intended international institution offers expertise unavailable locally. Study under internationally recognized experts or global leaders will significantly advance their field. International training will contribute meaningfully to their future academic or research career and ultimately benefit South Africa. title: TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 | Up to £25,000 for Higher Education Partnerships
summary: Higher education institutions seeking to strengthen international collaboration can now apply for the TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 under the Going Global Partnerships programme. The second round of funding offers 11 additional grants to support partnerships between institutions in the United Kingdom, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand. The grants aim to promote sustainable transnational education (TNE) partnerships that expand access to quality education, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to positive change in local education systems. About the TNE Exploratory Grants The TNE Exploratory Grants support innovative projects that explore opportunities for transnational education partnerships while promoting inclusive and accessible international education. The programme seeks to encourage institutions to better understand local educational contexts, develop sustainable partnerships, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through international education collaboration. Grant Objectives Projects should address one or more of the following objectives: * Promote long-term and sustainable institutional change through Transnational Education (TNE). * Increase access to high-quality and inclusive education. * Improve understanding of local contexts and regulatory environments that support TNE partnerships. * Strengthen operational frameworks for international education collaboration. * Support education initiatives that respond to local needs and priorities. * Contribute to positive changes in education systems and SDG achievement. Funding Details Grant Amount : Up to £25,000 * Project Duration: 17 months * Project Start Date : January 2027 * Number of Projects Funded : 11 * Programme: Going Global Partnerships Participating Countries : Armenia, Bangladesh, Thailand, and the United Kingdom Eligibility Criteria For Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships * The lead institution must be a UK higher education provider with degree-awarding powers. * Partnerships should involve eligible institutions in Armenia or Bangladesh. For Thailand Partnerships * The lead institution must be a Thai higher education institution . * Partnerships should involve eligible UK institutions and meet programme requirements. Applicants should consult the official Call Guidance document for complete eligibility requirements. Benefits of the Grant Selected institutions will receive: * Funding of up to £25,000. * Opportunities to establish or strengthen international partnerships. * Support for exploring sustainable TNE models. * Enhanced institutional capacity for international collaboration. * Opportunities to contribute to educational development and SDG-related outcomes. * Greater understanding of local educational systems and regulatory frameworks. Application Process Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform. Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships Applicants should use: Going Global Partnerships – Armenia Bangladesh – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead UK institution. Thailand Partnerships Applicants should use: Going Global Partnerships – Thailand – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead Thai institution. Important Dates Clarification Questions Deadline: 23 July 2026 Application Deadline: 2 September 2026, 11:59 a.m. BST Project Start Date: January 2027 Why Apply ? The TNE Exploratory Grants provide an excellent opportunity for universities and higher education institutions to explore innovative international education partnerships. Beyond financial support, the programme helps institutions build long-term collaboration frameworks that improve educational access, quality, and sustainability across multiple countries. Institutions interested in expanding their global engagement strategies and contributing to stronger international education systems should consider applying for this competitive funding opportunity. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform before the deadline. Application Deadline : 2 September 2026 Conclusion The TNE Exploratory Grants: Round 2 offer an excellent opportunity for higher education institutions in the UK, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand to build innovative international partnerships that can transform access to quality education. With funding of up to £25,000 per project, successful applicants will have the chance to explore new transnational education models, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to more inclusive and sustainable higher education systems. Beyond financial support, these grants provide a platform for institutions to deepen international engagement, improve understanding of local educational contexts, and develop initiatives that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The programme encourages institutions to create long-term impact by fostering knowledge exchange, enhancing educational opportunities, and supporting positive policy and system-level changes. If your institution is looking to establish or expand meaningful transnational education partnerships, this grant programme could be the catalyst needed to turn innovative ideas into impactful projects. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and application guidance before submitting their proposals ahead of the 2 September 2026 deadline.
